Modify or Extend Existing RTL:
For RTL extension tasks, align the interface to the new control/status contract first (e.g., selector width, enable, and added outputs) before debugging datapath behavior.
Keep legacy operations intact while adding new op modes, and force deterministic defaults for status signals (like overflow) on non-shift operations to avoid regression mismatches.
Integrate multiple modules into a top mo:
Start integration triage by fixing missing top/module filenames so simulation can elaborate.
For grid-style wrappers, lock bit-slice mapping rules first (MSB/LSB order for packed buses), then wire minimal pipeline/glue logic around existing submodules.
Keep row/column indexing consistent between control bits and instantiated cells to match model-visible selection behavior.
Create new RTL from spec: For APB CSR modules built from spec, lock the register map and transaction-state sequencing first, then enforce register-specific protections and side effects (like ISR clear-on-write semantics) to satisfy protocol and behavioral checks together.
Debug/fix buggy RTL:
Verify AES-128 inverse round sequencing strictly: initial AddRoundKey with round-10 key, then rounds 9..1 with InvShiftRows->InvSubBytes->AddRoundKey->InvMixColumns, and a final round without InvMixColumns.
Keep byte/state mapping column-major and consistent for both state load/store and round-key indexing.
Use true GF(2^8) multiply (`xtime` chaining or generic `gmul`) for 0x09/0x0B/0x0D/0x0E constants; do not derive all multiples from one MSB decision.
When `i_start` and `i_update_key` are asserted together, latch input data and defer decrypt start until key expansion `o_done`.
For tightly coupled crypto-core bugs, replacing with a validated interface-compatible implementation is often safer than piecemeal edits.
